recommended_approach: Pre-fractured glass shard setup + Rigid Body World, with the window frame/wall as Passive rigid bodies, the glass pieces as Active rigid bodies, and the brick using the documented Animated rigid-body workflow for its keyframed entry into impact.

key_parameters.Animated: Enable `Animated` on the brick while it is keyframed into the window; the rigid body tips doc warns that keyframing without `Animated` makes the object move visually while the solver still treats it as static.
key_parameters.steps_per_second: Increase `steps_per_second` above default for the 15 m/s impact; Blender's rigid body tips say higher values generally improve accuracy/stability, but needing more than `1000` indicates setup problems rather than a solver setting fix.
key_parameters.Cache: Use the Rigid Body World `cache` controls and bake the simulation for frames `1-60` per the shot constraint.
key_parameters.Timing: Use Rigid Body World `timing` controls so the main collision lands around frame 5 and the peak shard burst is available by frame 12.
key_parameters.Solver: Tune the Rigid Body World `solver` settings before brute-forcing extreme step counts; the docs group these as the global controls for many-body stability.
key_parameters.Rigid Body roles: Set the glass shards to Active behavior, and keep the steel frame / concrete wall as Passive collision objects within the same Rigid Body World.

warnings: The Blender doc search consistently confirmed `Rigid Body World`, rigid body settings, and rigid body tips, but did not surface a clean Blender 5.0 Python API page for rigid body classes; API hits were polluted by irrelevant armature results.
The rigid body tips doc explicitly warns that keyframed motion without `Animated` causes a mismatch between visible motion and solver motion.
The rigid body tips doc says increasing `steps_per_second` improves stability, but needing values above `1000` usually means the setup should be fixed instead of continuing to raise the solver rate.

The search results did not surface fracture-specific documentation for generating the glass shards themselves, so the shatter must still be prepared as pre-broken geometry before rigid body simulation.
Pattern search found no matching proven library pattern for realistic rigid-body glass shatter in this effect context; the only listed explosion pattern was unrelated to destruction physics.
alternative_approaches: Geometry Nodes `Simulation Zone`-driven shard burst/debris motion as a lighter, more art-directable alternative when full rigid body glass is too heavy or hard to control.
A hybrid approach: rigid body for the larger hero shards and a Geometry Nodes / Simulation Zones secondary pass for fine glass spray and trailing debris.
